plan: Trim SPY to 20% to meet the single-name concentration mandate and reduce broad index exposure.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets approximately 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, aiming for lower drawdowns. However, it will likely underperform in strong bull markets.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate and reduce overall broad index exposure.
Sell all SOXL and SPAL to significantly reduce leveraged ETF risk.
Trim SMH to 8% and CRWD to 10% to reduce semiconductor and AI/Software concentration.
Initiate a new position in GUSH at 5% based on its strong scanner read for diversification.

balanced.read: This balanced plan targets approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing some diversification. Expect moderate drawdowns, but also moderate growth potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate while maintaining significant broad index exposure.
Add to SOXL up to 5% to leverage strong semiconductor setups, adhering to the 15% combined limit.
Sell SPAL to remove an underperforming leveraged ETF.
Trim SMH to 10% to rebalance semiconductor exposure, shifting some to SOXL.
Initiate new positions in GUSH at 8% and MU at 7% based on their high scanner scores.
Maintain a smaller cash buffer of approximately 5% to maximize market exposure.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It utilizes and adds leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups, which significantly raises both upside and drawdown potential. Be aware that leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this approach can lead to substantial losses quickly if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and allow for a larger cash buffer.
Increase QQQI to 30% to significantly boost income ETF allocation for monthly distributions.
Sell all QQQ, SMH, and CRWD to reduce growth and high-beta exposure.
Sell all SOXL and SPAL to eliminate leveraged ETFs and high-risk positions.
Prioritize low drawdown and reliable income over growth, maintaining a substantial cash buffer.
The portfolio will be heavily weighted towards income-generating ETFs and broad index exposure.
income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1% per month, aiming to park cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income through income/covered-call ETFs and broad index exposure. Distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in selloffs, so this is not a savings account, but it focuses on steady monthly distributions.
